# Worktree Module-Resolution Isolation — Intake Brief

## Problem Statement

Two documentation gaps exist: `AGENTS.md` (global and repo copies) contains a
dangling link to `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, and the existing isolation
doc lacks a cross-reference to the node-modules-verification doc. This task
produces the final, authoritative documentation on how worktree module
resolution works and repairs all references.

## Users

- **Agents** running the implement workflow: they need one authoritative doc
  explaining the supported setup and the failure signatures to recognise.
- **Producers** reviewing `in_review` items: they need trust in the gate result
  (green means correct, red names the change).
- **Contributors** debugging stale-`dist` false-reds: they need the failure
  signature and the sanctioned refresh mechanism documented.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **New doc created.** `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` documents: (a) the
   module-resolution order in a worktree (node_modules symlink/link farm,
   `@worklog/shared` → main vs worktree `packages/shared`, `main`/`exports` →
   `dist`), (b) the supported way to make `packages/shared` changes visible
   (link farm from SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO), and (c) the stale-dist failure
   signature (e.g. the `spy never called` false red).
2. **AGENTS.md links fixed.** All references to `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
   in `AGENTS.md` and `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` resolve to an existing file (absolute
   path or correct relative path).
3. **Cross-reference added.** `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md`
   links to the new isolation doc.
4. **Constraints stated.** The implement skill's `npm install`-in-worktree ban
   and the no-writes-through-node_modules constraint are stated in the isolation
   doc.
5. **Validation passes.** Markdown link checks and the full project test suite
   pass with the changes.

## Constraints

- **Worktree isolation:** all changes must happen in an `implement.py` worktree.
  Do not edit from the main checkout.
- **No `npm install`** in the worktree (writes through the symlink corrupt the
  main checkout's `node_modules`).
- **Markdown links** must resolve from every document's perspective.

## Risks & Mitigations

- **Link portability:** `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is symlinked to SorraAgents'
  `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`. An absolute path to ContextHub's doc will not be
  portable. **Mitigation:** use an absolute path to the specific user's
  ContextHub checkout (the link is only readable, not served to others).
- **Scope creep:** the doc already exists and is comprehensive; do not rewrite
  it. Only add cross-references and fix links.
- **Stale SorraAgents doc:** SorraAgents has its own shorter version of the doc
  at `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`. The AGENTS.md link currently resolves
  to it. **Decision:** the link should point to ContextHub's more comprehensive
  version; verify the implement skill doesn't also link to the SorraAgents copy.

## Existing State

- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` already exists with substantial content
  (worktrees, sync temp worktrees, guards, filesystem-walk races, main-checkout
  deletions).
- `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md` exists but does not
  cross-reference the isolation doc.
- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` line 40 has `[docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md](docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md)` —
  a relative link that resolves from the repo root but not from the global
  install location.
- `AGENTS.md` in this repo root and `templates/AGENTS.md` do not currently link
  to the isolation doc (the task is about fixing existing dangling links).

## Related Work

- **WL-0MVLK2JNB002E9JQ** — Worktree tests resolve `@worklog/shared` to the main
  checkout's stale dist (the root cause of the problem this docs the fix for).
- **SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO** — SorraAgents item delivering the link-farm mechanism
  (the resolution fix; blocked-by).
- **WL-0MVWK20DK004TQZM** — Recurrence: `packages/shared` wiped from main checkout.
- **WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2** — Worktree node_modules verification (related doc).
- **WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO** — Verify persist write-detection regression tests
  (the `spy never called` false red example).

## Appendix

No clarifying questions — the work item description and related work provide
sufficient detail for implementation.

## Plan review findings (2026-11-02)

Effort/risk pre-check: **Small / Low** (below the planning threshold), so the
plan session reviewed the existing content instead of decomposing it. Review
outcome: **three open questions block completion** — see below. The item is
left at `intake_complete`, awaiting producer answers.

### Corrected existing state (verified during review)

- **`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` does not exist in this repository.** The global agent
  file `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to
  `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`; it is installed by
  **SorraAgents'** `scripts/install_pi.sh` (ContextHub has no such script).
  ContextHub `AGENTS.md` line 3 claims the install comes from "this
  repository's `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`" — inaccurate for ContextHub, and out of
  scope here unless the producer wants it corrected in this item.
- **Nothing to repair in ContextHub `AGENTS.md` / `templates/AGENTS.md`.**
  Neither contains a reference to `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, so the
  "dangling link" exists only in the SorraAgents copy of the global file (its
  relative link is dangling for a reader of `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`, while
  resolving fine inside the SorraAgents checkout).
- **ContextHub `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`** (~230 lines) covers
  implementation worktrees, sync temp worktrees, hook guards, main-checkout
  deletion detection/recovery and repo-wide-walk races, but has **no**
  module-resolution section.
- **`docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md`** has no link
  to the isolation doc (AC3 confirmed outstanding).
- **No markdown link checker exists in ContextHub** — `package.json` has no
  link/lint script and no doc-link test covers `docs/dev/*.md`. AC5's
  "Markdown link checks" therefore needs either one documented manual command
  or a small script/test added by the item.
- **AC4 constraints:** the `npm install`-in-worktree ban is already stated in
  isolation doc §1; the "no writes through `node_modules`" rule is only
  implied ("writes pass through the symlink and corrupt the shared tree"), not
  stated as a constraint.
- **AC1(b) mechanism does not exist yet:** `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` is still
  `open` / `plan_complete`, and `implement.py` today only provides
  `_ensure_node_modules_symlink` (plus nested workspace symlinks) — there is no
  link farm. Documentation would describe a workflow that cannot be followed
  yet.

### AC coverage review

| AC | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| AC1(a) resolution order | Ready | Main checkout's `node_modules/@worklog/shared` → `../../packages/shared`; `main`/`exports` → `./dist/*.js` (verified in `packages/shared/package.json`) |
| AC1(b) link-farm setup | **Blocked** | Depends on `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` (Q2) |
| AC1(c) stale-dist signature | Ready | "spy never called" false red — WL-0MVK6S4HM005GBCO |
| AC2 link repair | **Blocked** | Cross-repo target + authoritative-doc decision (Q1, Q3) |
| AC3 cross-reference | Ready | Small edit |
| AC4 constraints stated | Ready | Small edit |
| AC5 validation | Ready, with gap | No link checker exists; item must add one or document a manual check |

### OPEN QUESTION 1 — scope / repo split (producer, blocking)

AC2 spans two repositories: `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` lives in the SorraAgents
checkout, while this item's constraint requires all changes inside a ContextHub
`implement.py` worktree. Options:

- **A (recommended).** Keep AC2 here in scope but file a separate
  SorraAgents-scoped work item for the `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` edit; a cross-repo
  reference edit cannot ship from a ContextHub worktree.
- **B.** Reword AC2 to ContextHub only (add the isolation-doc link to
  ContextHub `AGENTS.md`) and file the global-link fix against SorraAgents.
- **C.** Explicitly authorise this item to edit both checkouts as a documented
  exception to the worktree constraint.

Why it matters: it determines whether implementation creates one worktree or
two, and whether a SorraAgents item must land first.

### OPEN QUESTION 2 — dependency on an unbuilt mechanism (producer, blocking)

AC1(b) must document the link-farm setup from `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO`, which is
not implemented (`implement.py` still only symlinks `node_modules`). Options:

- **A (recommended).** Mark this item `blocked` on `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` and
  implement once it lands, so the doc describes the mechanism as built and
  testable.
- **B.** Ship AC1(a)/(c), AC3, AC4 now and add AC1(b) as a follow-up child
  after SA lands.
- **C.** Document the intended mechanism now, explicitly labelled "not yet
  implemented".

Why it matters: documenting a non-existent setup would send agents down a path
that silently resolves to the main checkout's stale `dist` — the false-red /
false-green problem this doc is meant to prevent.

### OPEN QUESTION 3 — authoritative doc and link target (producer, blocking)

The intake states the `AGENTS.md` link should point at ContextHub's "more
comprehensive version", but the SorraAgents copy
(`SorraAgents/docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, 416 lines, including the RCA and
test-isolation references) is the longer document and is the one the framework
guidance actually ships with; ContextHub's doc is only longer in
ContextHub-specific guards (main-checkout recovery, walk races). Options:

- **A.** Global link → ContextHub doc by absolute path (as the intake states);
  the SorraAgents doc stays unchanged. Risk: the global agent file then depends
  on one user's checkout layout (the intake already accepts this).
- **B (recommended).** Global link → SorraAgents doc via a repo-portable
  reference (absolute path or a path that stays valid inside that checkout),
  and add the module-resolution section to ContextHub's doc with an explicit
  cross-link between the two.
- **C.** Keep both docs, cross-link them, and state in each which one is
  authoritative for what.

Why it matters: it decides which file AC1's module-resolution section is
authored in, and whether the global link is portable.

### Proposed sequencing (contingent on the answers)

1. Add the missing doc-link check (script or test) proving every `docs/dev/*.md`
   reference resolves — makes AC5 executable rather than manual.
2. Author the AC1 module-resolution section in the doc chosen by Q3.
3. Add the AC3 cross-reference and the AC4 constraint statements.
4. Repair the AC2 references in the repo(s) chosen by Q1, rebasing AC1(b) on
   `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` per Q2.

### Appendix — questions and answers

- Q: "AC2 spans two repositories (SorraAgents `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` vs this
  ContextHub worktree constraint) — which repo(s) should the fix land in?"
  Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer), no evidence yet; options A/B/C
  above.
- Q: "AC1(b) documents the link farm from `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO`, which is not
  implemented — block, split, or document as forward-looking?"
  Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Evidence:
  `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` stage `plan_complete`, `status: open`;
  `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` has `_ensure_node_modules_symlink`
  only.
- Q: "Which `worktree-isolation.md` is authoritative, and what should the
  global link point at?"
  Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (awaiting producer). Evidence: ContextHub doc 230
  lines vs SorraAgents doc 416 lines; `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` →
  `SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`.
- Prior answered input reused: intake Appendix states "No clarifying
  questions — the work item description and related work provide sufficient
  detail"; that holds for AC1(a)/(c), AC3, AC4 and does not pre-empt Q1–Q3.

## Plan decisions (2026-11-02) — producer answers and final scope

Producer answered the three open questions raised by the review:

- **Q1 → A.** Keep AC2 in scope here, and file a SorraAgents-scoped work item
  for the `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` edit → **`SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S`** ("Fix dangling
  worktree-isolation.md link in AGENTS_GLOBAL.md (absolute path + ContextHub
  cross-link)"). A global-file change cannot ship from a ContextHub worktree.
- **Q2 → "as you prefer".** Chosen: **B — ship what is ready now, defer the
  link-farm subsection.** Reasoned deviation from the option A I had
  recommended: `wl` reconciles `blocked` → `open` from the dependency-edge
  graph and cross-store edges cannot be recorded yet
  (WL-0MVWABT2Z001XMSD), so "mark blocked on the SA item" is not a mechanical
  hold here — it would silently look startable. Option B instead delivers
  AC1(a), AC1(c), AC3, AC4 and AC5 now and isolates AC1(b) in a child that
  carries an explicit producer hold.
- **Q3 → B.** The global `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` link targets **SorraAgents'**
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` via an absolute path; **this** repository's
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` carries the module-resolution section and
  cross-links the SorraAgents page (whose own ContextHub cross-link is in
  `SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S`).

### Scope map: acceptance criteria → work item

| AC | Where it is delivered |
|---|---|
| AC1(a) resolution order | `WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU` (module-resolution section) |
| AC1(b) link-farm setup | `WL-0MVZ4IJKL000VFEL` — held pending `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` |
| AC1(c) stale-dist signature | `WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU` |
| AC2 link repair | `SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S` (SorraAgents) — this item tracks it |
| AC3 cross-reference | `WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU` |
| AC4 constraints stated | `WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU` |
| AC5 validation | `WL-0MVZ4I4QR000C1UG` (adds the link check) + changed-scope gate |

### Children (test-first, dependency order)

1. **`WL-0MVZ4I4QR000C1UG`** — *Doc-link resolution check for `docs/dev` and
   `AGENTS.md`* (task; verification first, makes AC5 executable). Startable now.
2. **`WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU`** — *Add module-resolution section to
   `worktree-isolation.md` with AC3 cross-reference and AC4 constraints* (docs;
   depends on 1).
3. **`WL-0MVZ4IJKL000VFEL`** — *Document link-farm setup once
   `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` lands (AC1b)* (docs; depends on 2; held with
   `needsProducerReview=true` until the SA mechanism ships).

### Corrections to this brief's earlier sections

Where the sections above contradict the "Plan review findings" section, the
findings win: there is no `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` in this repository, ContextHub's
`AGENTS.md` / `templates/AGENTS.md` carry no isolation-doc reference to repair,
SorraAgents' copy of the doc is the longer one (not "shorter"), and no Markdown
link checker existed before child 1 created one.

### Sequencing notes for implementation

- Child 1 must land first: it is the verification for every subsequent link
  edit (test-first ordering).
- Child 2 keeps the existing isolation-doc sections untouched (intake risk:
  no rewrite) and adds the `Constraints` block rather than restating §1.
- Child 3 replaces child 2's "current vs pending" note with the shipped
  link-farm description — it must not be started before
  `SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` is `in_review`/`completed`.
- `SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S` is independent of children 1–3 and can proceed in
  parallel in the SorraAgents repository.

## Plan changelog (2026-11-05) — re-plan after the link-farm mechanism landed

Effort/risk pre-check: **Small / Low** → below the planning threshold (skip
path). The six review stages ran against the existing content; the 2026-11-02
decomposition is unchanged and reused (no new features invented, no duplicate
children). Only facts were refreshed.

### What changed since 2026-11-02

- **`SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` (SorraAgents, the link-farm mechanism) is now
  `completed` / `in_review`.** `implement.py start` materialises a
  worktree-local link farm (`_materialise_link_farm` /
  `_reconcile_link_farm`), overrides every path-consumed workspace package
  (`@worklog/shared` → the worktree's own `packages/shared`) and reports
  `shared_resolution` / `shared_resolution_ok` in its start JSON. AC1(b) is
  therefore no longer forward-looking: child 3 was re-planned to
  `plan_complete` and is implementable.
- **Child 1** `WL-0MVZ4I4QR000C1UG` (doc-link check) and **child 2**
  `WL-0MVZ4IIZD0010BQU` (module-resolution section + AC3 cross-reference +
  AC4 constraints) are `completed` / `done` (commits `a58a5818`,
  `905b46e1`) → AC1(a), AC1(c), AC3, AC4 and AC5 are delivered.
- **AC2 is delivered cross-repo.** `SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S` (SorraAgents) is
  `completed` / `in_review` (commit `721624cf6`); the installed
  `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` was verified to have zero dangling file links. No
  ContextHub-side work remains for AC2.
- **New fact found in review (folded into child 3, not a new child):**
  `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` §"Current vs pending: there is no link farm
  yet" and the subtitle/fix 1 of
  `docs/dev/implement-worktree-node-modules-verification.md` now describe the
  pre-fix world as current. Correcting both is the same edit on the same
  subject as child 3 → child 3's AC1b/AC4/AC5 and Key Files cover it.

### AC coverage review (2026-11-05)

`run_coverage_review` → `recommendation: auto_close`, coverage 20% (1 of 5
parent ACs). Every "gap" maps to an **already-completed** child AC:

| Parent AC | Matched child AC (completed) | Score |
|---|---|---|
| AC1 (new doc) | child 2 — "Resolution order documented (AC1a)" | 0.29 |
| AC2 (AGENTS.md links) | child 1 — "Check exists and runs in the default suite" | 0.23 |
| AC4 (constraints) | child 2 — "Constraints stated (AC4)" | 0.26 |
| AC5 (validation) | child 2 — "Links resolve and the suite is green" | 0.21 |

The scores fall below the 0.4 coverage threshold only because the parent ACs
are long compound sentences; the `resolved_gaps` mapping is semantically
correct. `apply_coverage_review` was therefore **deliberately not applied**: it
would create four `Close coverage gap: …` children that duplicate completed
work, which the plan skill's duplicate-detection rule forbids. The outcome is
recorded here instead — see OPEN QUESTION 4.

### OPEN QUESTION 4 — coverage gate vs duplicate creation (recorded, non-blocking; producer raised no objection)

Option A (taken) stands. Assumption recorded rather than invented: the producer
answered the hold-release question with **A** on 2026-11-05 and gave no
instruction on this question, so it is left as a documented deviation to be
revisited if the producer prefers B or C.

The helper reaches `auto_close` on this parent and would create four duplicate
children even though the semantic coverage is complete.

- **A (taken).** Advance to `plan_complete`, record the mapping above, create
  nothing. Risk: the gate's own record shows 20% coverage for a covered plan.
- **B.** Rewrite the parent `## Acceptance Criteria` as the seven-item
  decomposition the scope map below already defines. Risk: it inverts the gate
  (parent ACs copied from children) and drops the met-outside-the-tree AC2
  record.
- **C.** Accept the four auto-created children and close them as duplicates of
  the completed ones. Risk: four permanently closed duplicate items as noise.

### Appendix — questions and answers (2026-11-05)

- Q: "The link-farm mechanism (`SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO`) is now
  `completed`/`in_review`, which is exactly what child `WL-0MVZ4IJKL000VFEL`

  Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): **A — clear the hold now.** Final: A.
  Evidence: `wl show SA-0MVMZBJGT00718ZO` → `completed` / `in_review`;

- Prior answers reused, not re-asked: Q1 → A, Q2 → "as you prefer" → B,
  Q3 → B (all 2026-11-02, see "Plan decisions" above).

### Sequencing notes (unchanged)

- Children 1 and 2 already landed; child 3 is the only open child and must not

- `SA-0MVZ4BECY002X81S` (AC2) is complete; nothing awaits it.
- The parent stays `open` / `plan_complete` with its `Map` producer hold: a
  child is non-terminal, so the parent is not advanced to `in_review`.

## Plan changelog (2026-11-10, second session) — re-verified, no plan changes

Effort/risk pre-check: **Small / Low** → below the planning threshold (skip
path). The six review stages were re-run against the existing content; nothing
had changed since the 2026-11-10 review, so no description, AC or child edits

### Verified this session

  (module-resolution section + AC3 cross-reference + AC4 constraints,
  `completed`/`done`), `WL-0MVZ4IJKL000VFEL` (AC1b link-farm subsection,
  `open`/`plan_complete`, dispatchable, no producer hold).
- **Dependency chain intact:** 3 → 2 → 1 (verification child first, test-first

- **Delivered artefacts present in the tree:** `tests/docs/dev-link-check.test.ts`,

# Intake Brief: Herdr Package Tests Excluded from Full Suite

## Headline

Herdr package tests (~151 files) are excluded from the configured full test suite. The producer has already decided (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8) to accept this gap — this item captures the residual question of whether the herdr group gate is adequate and whether the decision is properly documented.

## Problem Statement

The herdr package tests (~151 test files in `packages/herdr/src/`) are excluded from the configured full test suite (`suiteCommands` in `.pi/test-config.json`). While the producer has already decided not to include herdr tests in the full suite (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8), the residual question is whether the `herdr` group gate provides adequate coverage and whether the decision is properly documented.

## Users

- **Agent developers**: Need to know that herdr tests are gated (via the `herdr` group) even if not in the full suite.
- **Producer/operator**: Needs to ensure the herdr group gate is sufficient for their confidence requirements.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The producer's prior decision (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8: "herdr tests will not be run as part of the canonical full suite") is confirmed and documented on this work item.
2. The `herdr` group in `.pi/test-config.json` is confirmed as the active gate for herdr package tests.
3. The herdr group command (`npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`) is verified to run all 151 herdr test files.
4. If the herdr group is inadequate, a follow-up work item is created for the producer's review.
5. Full project test suite must pass with the changes.

## Constraints

- Current `suiteCommands` is `["npm --silent test -- tests"]` — only covers root `tests/`.
- Herdr tests run via `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src` (vitest scoped to that directory).
- Herdr test group is defined in `.pi/test-config.json` under `groups.herdr`.
- The producer has already declined to include herdr tests in the full suite.

## Existing State

- `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands`: only `tests/` directory.
- `groups.herdr` defined with command `npm --silent test -- packages/herdr/src`.
- Herdr tests (~151 files) run only via `--group herdr` or bare `npm test`.
- WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8: producer explicitly declined full-suite inclusion.

## Key Files

- `.pi/test-config.json` — test suite configuration; may need documentation update.
- `vitest.config.ts` — vitest configuration; no changes needed.
- `packages/herdr/src/` — herdr package source and test files.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8**: "Canonical full suite excludes the herdr package tests" — **completed, won't fix**. Producer explicitly decided herdr tests should not run in the canonical full suite.
- **WL-0MVP643Q4007BZJ8**: Environment-dependent flake in herdr tests — the motivating incident for this work item.
- **WL-0MLXLTPXI1NS29OZ**: Update existing pre-filter tests (completed).
- **docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md**: Test suite baseline documentation.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: The herdr group gate might be missed by agents who only check `--scope full` without checking group coverage. Mitigation: document clearly.

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B — decompose `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `worklist.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely without touching any existing test file and
without a reviewer having to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 require: every production module ≤1,000 lines, an
unchanged public surface at `./worklist.js`, unmodified test files, no new
circular imports, and a single `WorkItemListState` declaration. Nothing in the
repo enforces these for `worklist.ts` today. The `downtime-worker` series
already built exactly this machinery for its own split
(`packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` + `downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts`);
this child reuses it rather than duplicating it.

- **36 consumer files** import from `./worklist.js`/`./worklist`: 2 production
  (`index.ts` → `getTermSize`, `runWorklistTui`; `fetcher.ts` → `STAGES`,
  `Stage`) and 34 test files, of which **24** are `worklist*.test.ts` suites.
- **66 distinct symbols** are imported across those consumers; the other 23 of
  the 89 current exports are unused outside the module and become internal
  (parent AC2).
- `WorkItemListState` is declared **once** (`worklist.ts:490`) — the single
  owner AC5 protects.
- `runWorklistTui` is declared once (`worklist.ts:5581`, `export async function`)
  and must stay at the `./worklist.js` path with an identical signature
  (child WL-0MVND6MQS000L01W).
- The live static import graph already contains one large component that
  includes `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
  (`CYCLE_BASELINE` in `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`). It is
  pre-existing and out of scope; what the gate forbids is a **new** cycle member
  or a new **runtime** cycle (parent AC4).

1. New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-guard.test.ts`
   (vitest) exists and passes on the current tree **before any production code
   moves**; no existing test file is modified (parent AC3).
2. Committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/worklist.split-baseline.json` records
   the 66 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation command,
   source commit, timestamp, scanned globs).
3. **Public-surface gate:** every baseline symbol is still exported by
   `./worklist.js` (value or type), and every symbol the live consumers import
   from the barrel is exported by it — so a lost or trimmed re-export fails the
   suite (parent AC2).
4. **Single state-owner gate:** exactly one production
   `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module declares `WorkItemListState`
   (parent AC5), mirroring the `dispatchInFlightCount` gate.
5. **Barrel/cycle gate:** no production `worklist.*.ts` module contains a
   runtime (value) import of `./worklist.js` (nor of `./index.js`); the static
   import graph of `worklist*.ts` modules contains no cycle outside the recorded
   baseline allowlist (parent AC4).
6. **Size gate:** every production `packages/herdr/src/worklist*.ts` module is
   ≤1,000 lines, excluding an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains
   only `'worklist.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever
   shrinks (it must remain a subset of the plan-time list). The final barrel
   child empties it (parent AC1).
7. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a duplicated
   `WorkItemListState`, a new cycle) — the failure modes are unit-tested, not
   assumed.
8. **Reuse, do not fork, the scanner:** extend
   `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` minimally so the barrel path, the
   module-family matcher and the single-owner declaration name are injectable
   (each defaulting to today's `downtime-worker` behaviour). The existing
   `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.split-guard.test.ts` and

9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite and the
   untouched `downtime-worker` guard.
10. A comment on this item records the baseline generation command and the
    gate-to-parent-AC mapping.

1. Parametrise `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts`: accept a
   `barrel`/`family`/`declarationName` target (defaults unchanged) in

2. Generate the baseline: scan `src/**/*.ts` + `packages/herdr/src/*.ts` for

3. Write `worklist.split-guard.test.ts` with the five gates (exports,

4. Add the negative-case fixtures (temp files under `os.tmpdir()` or inline

5. Export `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` from the guard's helper section so the final child

6. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope); record the guard output in a comment.

## Goal

As a producer browsing the Herdr worklog selection list, I want the items that **block** a visible blocked item to also be **visible**, and in the **same group** as the blocked item, so that I can see (and dispatch) the work that must be finished before the blocked work can start — instead of seeing "blocked" rows whose blockers are nowhere in the list.

**Reported symptom (llm-proxy worklog):** `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4`, `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` and `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` are visible in the Herdr selection list, but their blocking items are not visible anywhere in the list.

**Discovered from:** llm-proxy work items `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` (Group 1 validation), `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` (Group 2 validation) and `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` (Optimise llama-server prefill latency). Those ids are foreign to this store; they are listed only as evidence.

## Reproduction (measured 2026-11-08)

Selection list for the llm-proxy worklog (`/home/rgardler/projects/llm`), with `browseItemCount = 20` (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`):

| Visible blocked item | Stage | Active blocker(s) (status / stage / parent) |
|---|---|---|
| `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` | intake_complete | `LP-0MW7V292T0020G02` open / intake_complete / **root**, `LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI` open / intake_complete / **root** |
| `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` | intake_complete | `LP-0MW7V2D13004ZO65` open / intake_complete / **root**, `LP-0MW7V2DK400365ER` open / intake_complete / **root**, `LP-0MW7V0S6A006DKZ4` (blocked — already visible) |
| `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` | plan_complete | `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ` open / intake_complete / **child of the blocked item** |
| `LP-0MW0KZVRX005VPMT` | idea | `LP-0MW7V14DN007F127` (blocked — already visible) |

Verified by driving the **real** functions against the live data: build the pipeline input from `wl worklist -n 20 --json` (browse feed + `critical`/`reviewQueue`/`inProgressRoots`/`blockedRoots` subsets, deduped by id), then call `selectWorkItems(merged, 20)` and `regroupWorkItems(selected)` from `packages/herdr/src/`. Result: **24 rows selected — 4 `blocked` rows plus 20 `In Review` rows — and every one of the three root blockers (`LP-0MW7V292T0020G02`, `LP-0MW7V29MA009MCPI`, `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ`) absent (HIDDEN)**. Grouping of that output: the four blocked items each sat in their own group (`Group 1`, `Group 2`, `Group 3`, `Idea`), the 20 in_review rows in `In Review`.

## Root cause 1 — the browse window is fully consumed by the mandatory review queue

1. `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (`fetcher` wrapper) calls `fetchNextItems(clampBrowseItemCount(settings.browseItemCount))` — 20 here; the plugin default is also 20.
2. `fetchNextItems` → `assembleDefaultWorklist` / `mergeMandatoryAndSelect` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`) → `selectWorkItems(merged, count)`.
3. `selectWorkItems` (`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`) always includes the mandatory set (critical ∪ `status=in-progress` ∪ `status=blocked` ∪ completed `in_review`) and then fills only `othersLimit = max(0, count − mandatory.length)` slots with everything else.
4. **A blocker is only ever an "other".** `isMandatoryItem` never matches an `open` item, and nothing in the pipeline looks at dependency edges. With 20 root completed/in_review items + 4 blocked roots in this worklog, `othersLimit = 0`, so **every** non-mandatory item is cut — including every open blocker. (This is not blocker-specific: right now the window is entirely saturated by the review queue. The blocker case is the sharpest symptom because the blockers are the items the blocked rows are waiting on.)

## Root cause 2 — no blocker→blocked grouping rule

`groupItemsByFilePaths` (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`) gives **every** item with no `Key Files` section its own singleton "restricted" group. None of the items in the table above has a `Key Files` section, so even if a blocker were selected it would land in a *different* group (and its own section heading) from the blocked item it blocks. There is no rule anywhere that associates a dependency edge with group membership: edges are read only for the metadata panel's `Blocked By` rows (`fetchBlockersForItem` / `fetchOutboundDepsForItems` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts`).

## Root cause 3 — a child blocker is excluded by the root-only top-level rule

`LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ` is a **child of the blocked item it blocks** (`LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT`). `selectWorkItems` drops every item with a non-empty `parentId` (root-only top level, `WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR` / `WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI`), so that blocker is only reachable by expanding the parent — where it does render inside the parent's group.

**The fix must keep that rule.** A blocker that is a child is never promoted to the top level; it is represented by its **ROOT ancestor** (the same parent-substitution contract the critical-child path already implements — `substituteCriticalRoots` / `walkToRootAncestor` in `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`, `WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI`). When the child blocker's root ancestor *is* the blocked item itself (exactly the `LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` → `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ` case) substitution collapses to an item that is already visible: nothing is added, nothing is duplicated, and the child stays reachable through expand inside the parent's group.

## Scope

**In:** the Herdr **default** worklist selection + regroup pipeline (`smart-selection.ts`, `fetcher.root-substitution.ts`, `grouping.ts`, and the blocker read they reuse); the tests named below; the doc/comment updates that state the new guarantee.

**Out:**
- **Stage-filtered views** (`fetchItemsByStage`): these are deliberately narrow, so injecting a blocker whose stage falls outside the filter would be wrong. The new guarantee is documented as default-view only.
- **Any change to the "show parents, not children" rule itself.** Children are never rendered at the top level; a child blocker is represented by its root ancestor (see Root cause 3 and AC6).
- **The `browseItemCount` policy itself** (a deep review queue starving every "other" item). If that is judged worth changing, raise it as a separate `discovered-from` item — this item only guarantees blocker visibility.
- The Pi TUI Worklog extension (its grouping copy was removed by `WL-0MSGI7PV9004UD0N`).
- `wl` core CLI grouping/scoring — the fix is Herdr-side only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Blocker visibility (the reported defect).** For a selection list built from the current live shape (20 root completed/in_review items, 4 blocked roots, `browseItemCount = 20`), every **active** blocker of a **visible** blocked item is represented in the returned list — as the blocker itself when it is a root item, or via its root ancestor when it is a child (AC6). A test reproduces the §Reproduction shape exactly (20 in_review + 4 blocked + open blockers) in `fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` against a seeded real worklog DB, and asserts each root blocker id is selected — not merely "not dropped by the count window".
- **AC2 — Same group as the blocked item.** Each pinned blocker carries the *same* `group` and `groupLabel` as the blocked item it blocks, despite having no shared key files. If a blocker blocks two or more visible blocked items that land in different groups, it appears **exactly once, in the first (lowest-numbered) group in display order**.
- **AC3 — Adjacency.** Within the group, a pinned blocker is placed immediately after the blocked item it was pinned for (deterministic: the lowest-numbered group's blocked item when it blocks several), so a blocked row is always followed by its blockers. If implementation cost forces a downgrade to "same group, anywhere in it", record that decision in a comment on this item rather than silently dropping the requirement.
- **AC4 — No duplicates, no disappearances.** The selected list contains no duplicate ids (a blocker already selected in an earlier group is not re-added), and no item that is visible today becomes invisible as a result of the change (pin-only, never remove).
- **AC5 — No-op when nothing is blocked.** When no visible item has an active blocker, the selected list and its grouping are byte-identical to today's output (regression test over a fixture with no blocked items).
- **AC6 — "Show parents, not children" preserved by parent substitution.** A blocker that is a **child** of another item is never rendered at the top level. Instead its **ROOT ancestor** (walk `parentId` to the top-most non-child item) is what gets pinned into the blocked item's group, reusing the existing `walkToRootAncestor` / `substituteCriticalRoots` machinery rather than a second implementation. Tests must cover three cases:
  - **child blocker under a third-party parent** → the root is pinned and the child id never appears at top level;
  - **child blocker whose root is the blocked item itself** (`LP-0MVMHNUAR006SRZT` / `LP-0MVNBJWG6006Z7YQ`) → no row is added at all (the substitute is already visible), no duplicate, and the child is still reachable via expand of the parent;
  - **nested child blocker** → the TOP-MOST ancestor is pinned (mirroring the existing nested-critical-child test).
  Also assert no leftover `parentId` item appears in the selected list at all (a generalisation of the existing root-only assertion), and that the existing critical-child substitution tests (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts`) still pass unchanged.
- **AC7 — One active-blocker predicate.** Pinning uses the shared `isActiveBlocker` predicate (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.blockers.ts`) so the pinned set can never disagree with the metadata panel's `Blocked By` rows: `completed`/`deleted` targets and targets at stage `in_review`/`done` are **not** pinned. Test covers each terminal case.
- **AC8 — Read cost.** Pinning adds **no** new `wl` process spawn per visible blocked item on the default path: reuse the in-process outbound-dep read (`fetchOutboundDepsForItems`, one batched read over all selected blocked ids) or extend the consolidated `wl worklist` bundle. State the measured spawn count before/after for the default refresh (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher-spawn-cap.test.ts` / split-guard suites stay green).
- **AC9 — Content-determinism preserved.** Group assignment remains a pure function of item content + dependency edges, never of `updatedAt`/arrival order (`WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO`): the same item set and edges always produce the same pinned grouping (test: shuffle the input, assert identical group numbers).
- **AC10 — Dispatch head stated and tested.** `getHerdrListHead` derives from the same selection, so pinning changes the dispatcher's candidate ranking. Record the intended effect (blockers become dispatchable from the list head) in a comment/doc, and cover it with a test so the ordering change is deliberate rather than incidental.
- **AC11 — Docs.** Update the mandatory-subset / selection documentation (`docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`) and the header comments of `smart-selection.ts` / `grouping.ts` to state: blockers of a visible blocked item are always shown, in the blocked item's group, first group wins, default view only.
- **AC12 — Deliberate invariant override documented.** Pinning overrides the file-path conflict invariant for the blocker/blocked pair (two conflicting items can share a group). Add the inline comment explaining why, so a later reader does not "fix" it back.

## Decisions already taken

- **"First group in the list"** means the lowest `group` integer, i.e. display order.
- **A child blocker is represented by its parent, never itself** (AC6) — the rule is "show parents, not children". The replacement is the **root ancestor** (top-most item), matching the critical-child precedent, not merely the immediate parent; promoting the child would re-introduce the duplicated-row bug that `WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR` / `WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI` removed. Where the substituted root is the blocked item itself the pin is a no-op (no duplicate row).
- **Pinning beats file-path packing** for the blocker/blocked pair (the user requirement), documented per AC12.
- Only **direct** blockers are pinned. A pinned blocker that is itself blocked is not chased transitively unless it is already mandatory — keep the rule simple and documented; transitive closure can be a follow-up if it proves necessary.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.blockers.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-visibility.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts`
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md`

## Related

- `WL-0MV71WBHB007D8ZE` — blocked items made mandatory (the reason the blocked rows are visible while their blockers are not).
- `WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8`, `WL-0MVBMLY2Z0032CYR` — `Blocked By` metadata rows (per-item only; no list membership).
- `WL-0MS964SIA0057ABR`, `WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI` — root-only top level / critical-child root substitution (AC6 must not regress these).
- `WL-0MVVLBTTP003Y4XO` — content-deterministic group assignment (AC9).
- `WL-0MVI0HX58009JJRF` — `wl worklist` consolidated read (the natural place to add batched blocker edges if AC8 is met there).

# Audit over-subscribed dialog is incorrect

## Problem statement

The herdr selection list's over-quota confirmation dialog (shown when the operator presses `a-a` to fire `/skill:audit` while the audit tier is at/over its host cap) reports a stale/inflated audit count. The worklist header counter was recently fixed to exclude dead (pane-gone) audit entries, but the dialog still uses the old admission-count rule, so the two surfaces disagree: the header says `audit 0/1` while the dialog claims `1 running, max 1`.

## Users

- **Herdr operators** firing audits by hand from the selection list. Example user story: "As an operator who just saw `[budget: implement 0/2 · audit 0/1]` in the header, when I press `a-a` to run an audit I expect the over-quota dialog — if shown at all — to quote the same audit count I just saw, not a phantom `1 running`."

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-dialog.ts` — renders the over-quota dialog from `HostBudgetPromptRequest { kind, live, max }`; quotes `live` verbatim ("(`<live>` running, max `<max>`) — over by `<overshoot>`").
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` — `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` decides whether to prompt. It computes the tier count via `readTierCount`, which for the audit tier calls `freshCount` (marker-compatible: every fresh entry counts, no live-pane requirement).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — `readHostBudgetStatus` (the header counter) uses `reduceAuditDisplayCounts`, a **pane-aware** display rule: a fresh confirmed entry whose `paneId` is absent from the trusted live pane list is excluded. This was introduced by WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV ("Audit budget header must not count a dead (pane-gone) audit entry", completed 2026-11-09).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — `freshCount`/`reduceMarkerCounts` (admission, marker-compatible) vs `reduceAuditDisplayCounts` (display, pane-aware) are intentionally different reductions.
- Combined consequence: the **display** count and the **admission** count can differ by exactly the dead-pane entries. The interactive dialog quotes the admission count, so it reads higher than the header.

## Desired change

Make the interactive over-quota dialog quote the same audit count the operator sees in the worklist header — i.e. the pane-aware **display** count — while leaving the dispatcher's admission semantics (fail-closed, marker-compatible) untouched.

Concretely: in `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch`'s count path for the audit tier, use the pane-aware display reduction (the same one `readHostBudgetStatus` uses) to populate both the prompt decision and the `live` value quoted in `HostBudgetPromptRequest`, so:

- a fresh audit entry whose `paneId` is absent from the trusted live pane list is **not** counted in the dialog (and does not, on its own, trigger the prompt);
- an unconfirmed audit entry (no `paneId`, reserve→spawn window) is still counted;
- an audit entry whose pane is live is still counted;
- stale entries stay excluded;
- the implement tier's counting is unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The over-quota dialog's audit `live` count matches the worklist header's audit display count for the same ledger and live pane list (the two surfaces no longer disagree).
- A dead (confirmed) audit entry whose `paneId` is absent from the live pane list does not trigger the over-quota dialog and is not quoted in it; an unconfirmed fresh audit entry and a fresh audit entry with a live pane still trigger/count; stale entries are excluded.
- Dispatcher admission (`readAuditBudgetState`/`freshCount`/`admitHostDispatch`) is unchanged: fail-closed, marker-compatible counting, 2 h staleness release.
- The implement-tier dialog behaviour and counts are unchanged.
- Unit tests pin the dialog-vs-header agreement (dead / live / unconfirmed / stale audit entries) and the unchanged admission behaviour.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents that the interactive dialog's audit display count follows the header's pane-aware rule.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Operators see the same audit count in the over-quota dialog as in the worklist header, so firing `a-a` no longer pops a phantom "1 running" prompt when no audit is actually in flight.

## Constraints

- Must not change dispatcher admission semantics (fail-closed; `maxAudit` governs dispatcher ticks).
- Must keep the display read read-only (no ledger reap/rewrite from the dialog path).
- The live pane list must remain a trusted machine-wide read; an absent list must fall back to the freshness rule (as the header does) rather than inventing a zero.
- No new dependencies; reuse existing pure reductions.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.ts` — switch the audit-tier count fed to the prompt from `freshCount` to the pane-aware display reduction (needs the live pane list it already reads).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.interactive.test.ts` — pin dialog-vs-header agreement and the dead/live/unconfirmed/stale cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts` — reuse `reduceAuditDisplayCounts` (no new reduction unless a shared helper is warranted).
- `packages/herdr/src/host-budget-status.ts` — reference for the pane-aware display rule.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — document the dialog's display-count rule.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (default):** Only the dialog's audit count is changed. The dispatcher's admission logic, the header counter, and the implement tier are untouched. If further alignment is desired (e.g. implement tier using display count in the dialog), file as a separate item.
- **Count divergence trade-off:** After the change, the dialog may not prompt at all when only dead-pane entries are present — the operator can fire an audit that admission (marker-compatible) would refuse. This is intentional: the operator sees the count they saw in the header and is making an informed choice.
- **Assumption:** The live pane list is already read in `prepareInteractiveAgentDispatch` and is available for the audit-tier display count. No new subprocess calls needed.

## Related work

- **WL-0MW8D4UQH002TWJV** — "Audit budget header must not count a dead (pane-gone) audit entry" (completed): introduced the pane-aware display rule for the header. This item makes the dialog follow the same rule.
- **WL-0MW5KC8J300942EA** — parent of the above (sweep/release backstop for closed panes).
- **WL-0MVXY0Z93002HKCZ** — the F4 interactive over-quota dialog (origin of the count source this item corrects).
- **WL-0MVXWQFGV000D2AB** — parent host dispatch budget work.
- **WL-0MTOFAUCH00217XL** – "Fix: derive header count from WorkItem rows only" (completed): header-count derivation (worklist list rows, not budget). Related header-count correctness precedent.
- **WL-0MW454I1X009Q17E** – "Group counts are incorrect" (open): another selection-list count surface. Related display-count correctness.
- **WL-0MTOFANL6004M3TY** – "Test: header count excludes heading rows" (completed): test precedent for header-count correctness.

### Related docs

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — documents the host dispatch budget, the F4 dialog and the pane-aware audit display rule.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — herdr plugin overview.
- `CLI.md` — CLI reference.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive questions were required — the bug and its root cause were fully resolvable from the repository and worklog.

## Context

Parent: WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS — herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget.

So this child **pins the client-side contract before the server exists**, exactly as the reserve-handshake slice C1 did (`downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts` header: types + tolerant parser first, client second, "NOTHING here is called on the dispatch path yet").

## Scope

Provisional wire contract (one constant, one parser, no behaviour change):

- `AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH = '/llama/local/audit/status'` in `downtime-worker.constants.ts` (documented as provisional; the proxy's final path is a one-line change).
- `AuditAvailability` type: `{ cap: number; live: number; available: boolean; leases?: AuditAvailabilityLease[]; reclaimed?: number }` plus the refusal-reason token the proxy uses.
- `parseAuditAvailabilityResponse(raw, httpStatus): AuditAvailability | null` — fail-closed tolerant parse with alias accessors for the fields whose names are not yet fixed (`cap|max|max_audit`, `live|in_flight|live_leases`, `available|can_admit`), lease entries carrying an expiry, and `null` for every unusable payload (never a permissive default).
- Tests: table-driven fixtures pinning grant / saturated / malformed / alias spellings / absent lease array / negative or non-finite numbers / non-object bodies.
- Documentation of the provisional contract and the 2026-11-10 probe result in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

No production call site consumes the parser in this child (no behaviour change).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH`, the `AuditAvailability` (and lease) types and `parseAuditAvailabilityResponse` exist in a new module `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`, exported from the barrel only where the later children need them.
- The parser maps a valid payload to `{ cap, live, available, leases? }`, taking `available` from the proxy's own field and never deriving a permissive value from missing data.
- Alias tolerance is pinned: each documented alias spelling parses to the same typed result, and an unrecognised-but-valid extra field is ignored (additive evolution).
- Malformed input (non-object, missing/non-finite/negative `cap` or `live`, `leases` not an array) returns `null` — a garbage payload can never be read as "available".
- A table-driven test file pins every case, and no production dispatch path imports the parser yet (asserted by a test).
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` records the provisional contract, that the proxy side is LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK, and the 2026-11-10 probe result (endpoint absent on the live proxy).
- Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

1. Add the constants + types + pure parser module (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`).
2. Add the table-driven contract test (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.test.ts`).
3. Add the barrel re-export following the existing `downtime-worker.local-reservation.contract.ts` pattern.
4. Add the provisional-contract + probe paragraph to `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`.

- **Assumption:** the proxy will expose cap, live leases and an availability verdict on one GET (per the parent's AC1 wording; the sibling item owns the exact shape).

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts`
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`


## Impact

Operators can stop worrying that a malformed or legacy proxy response will be misread as audit capacity: every payload the future audit gate cannot trust is rejected outright, and a field or path rename on either side stays a one-line change.

# Add the fail-closed audit-availability client

## Context

Parent: WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS — herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget.
Prerequisite: the pinned wire contract (`downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`).

The counterpart of `createLocalReserver` (`downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts`) and `createDowntimePoller` (`downtime-worker.poller.ts`): one bounded GET of the proxy's audit availability, with the failure classification **spelled out as a typed outcome** so the dispatcher's policy (fail closed, named reason) never has to guess from an empty value.

## Scope

`createAuditAvailabilityClient(proxyUrl, fetcher = globalThis.fetch, timeoutMs = DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS)` returning a client that resolves one typed outcome per call:

- `{ status: 'ok', availability }` — 2xx with a parseable payload.
- `{ status: 'endpoint-absent', reason: 'http-404' }` — the proxy predates the endpoint (the sibling item has not shipped).
- `{ status: 'unreachable', reason: 'timeout' | 'network' | 'http-<status>' }` — the proxy could not be reached or answered an unusable status.
- `{ status: 'unparsable', reason: 'bad-body' }` — 2xx with a body the pinned parser rejects.

The client never throws; the URL is normalised with the same trailing-slash convention as the reserve client; the abort timer is always cleared.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `createAuditAvailabilityClient` exists in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts` and resolves exactly the four typed outcomes above, never throwing.
- `GET` is used, the URL is `{proxyUrl}{AUDIT_AVAILABILITY_PATH}` with a normalised trailing slash, and the request is bounded by the timeout (abort is asserted in a test).
- `404` classifies as `endpoint-absent`; a `5xx`, a non-JSON body, a network rejection and an abort all classify as `unreachable`/`unparsable` with the reason naming the failing exchange.
- A 2xx payload the parser rejects is `unparsable` — never `ok` with partial data.
- Tests inject a fake fetcher and cover every outcome, the URL normalisation, the method/header, and the timer cleanup (no open handle after the call).
- Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Implement the client in `downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts` (reuse `DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS`).
2. Add the injected-fetcher test file following `downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`.
3. Re-export from the barrel where the dispatcher deps are wired.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the availability read is cheap enough to call once per audit candidate per tick (the current `readAuditBudgetState` pre-check is a local file read; the proxy read adds one local-network GET). If tick cost becomes a problem, a short-lived cache is a follow-up item, not scope here.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.contract.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.local-reservation.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.reserve.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.constants.ts`

## Impact

Operators can now tell, in one typed outcome, whether the proxy refused an audit because the budget is full, whether it has not shipped the endpoint yet, or whether the proxy is unreachable or answering garbage — so a fail-closed audit hold names the real cause instead of looking like an empty value.

# Audit gate reads proxy availability

## Context

Parent: WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS — herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget.
Prerequisites: the pinned contract and the availability client.

Today `getActiveAudit` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`) consults `readAuditBudgetState` (`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`), which reads the **per-host** `~/.herdr/downtime/budget.json` `maxAudit` cap plus the machine-scoped `dispatch-budget.json` ledger. Two ContextHub hosts therefore each believe they are under cap while both contend for the single local `llama-server` GPU — the 2026-11-03 incident.

This child makes the **audit tier only** proxy-derived; the implement tier is untouched.

## Scope

- Inject the availability read into the worker deps (`readAuditAvailability` seam on `DowntimeWorkerDeps`), wired in `main()` as `createAuditAvailabilityClient(runSettings.downtimeProxyUrl)` — the same wiring point as `reserveLocalCapacity`.
- `getActiveAudit` audit tier: query the proxy availability and map it to the result — `available === false` → `{ ok: true, active: true, source: 'proxy', reason: 'audit-budget-saturated', budget: { live, max: cap } }`; `available === true` → `{ ok: true, active: false, source: 'proxy' }`.
- The audit tier no longer asserts `budget.json` `maxAudit`; `readAuditBudgetState` is not called on the proxy path.
- Typed result changes in `downtime-worker.types.ts`: `source` gains `'proxy'`, `reason` gains `'audit-budget-saturated'` and `'audit-budget-unknown'`; the proxy's own token vocabulary is reused verbatim (one spelling shared with the proxy, no local renaming).
- Fail-closed mapping (AC3): `endpoint-absent` / `unreachable` / `unparsable` → `{ ok: true, active: true, source: 'proxy', reason: 'audit-budget-unknown' }` with the proxy error detail carried for the decision log — audit dispatch stops, with a named reason, instead of silently reverting to the per-host cap.
- The per-worklog dispatch-marker single-flight check below the host-wide check is retained unchanged (it answers a different question: "has this worklog already been audited this window").

## Acceptance Criteria

- For the audit tier, `getActiveAudit` returns `source: 'proxy'` with the proxy's verdict and evidence, and a test proves `budget.json` `maxAudit` (any value, including `0`) does not influence the proxy-path decision.
- A proxy `available: false` verdict yields `active: true, reason: 'audit-budget-saturated'` carrying the proxy's `live`/`cap` as `budget` evidence.
- An unreachable/absent/unparsable proxy yields `active: true, reason: 'audit-budget-unknown'` with the failing exchange recorded (timeout / network / http-404 / bad-body) — never a permissive `active: false`.
- The audit-path refusal tokens are defined once (`audit-budget-saturated`, `audit-budget-unknown`) with a literal-value test shared with the proxy's vocabulary, and the proxy path no longer produces the legacy `host-budget-audit` / `audit-host-saturated` tokens (asserted by a test).
- The implement tier is provably unchanged: `admitHostDispatch` still refuses/permits on `budget.json` `maxImplement` and the local ledger, and its existing tests pass unmodified.
- The availability read is invoked once per audit gate evaluation (a test counts the calls), and the deps seam is optional so every existing test double keeps compiling (a missing seam fails closed as `audit-budget-unknown`, not open).
- Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC1 — Audit admission is proxy-derived.** For the audit tier only, `getActiveAudit` / the dispatch gate queries the proxy's audit-availability endpoint (cap, live leases, available) and does not assert the local `budget.json` cap. The implement tier keeps its existing per-host budget (out of scope).
- **AC2 — One vocabulary, no disagreement.** The refusal reason token and log vocabulary match the proxy's (`audit-budget-saturated`), so a dispatcher admission and a proxy refusal cannot disagree; a divergence is logged with both sides' evidence.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Add the `readAuditAvailability` seam to `DowntimeWorkerDeps` (+ the barrel wiring in `main()`).
2. Extend `DowntimeActiveAuditResult` (`source: 'proxy'`, the two new reason tokens) and the decision-log vocabulary constants.
3. Rewrite the host-wide branch of `getActiveAudit` to consume the seam and map outcomes (fail closed on every non-`ok` outcome).
4. Export/propagate the token so `downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts` reports it as today's `audit-host-saturated` is reported.
5. Add scenario tests to `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` and the seam-wiring test in `index.downtime-select.test.ts`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** the proxy read adds one local GET per audit gate evaluation. Mitigated by the fact that the gate is already evaluated once per tick.
- **Risk (accepted by design, parent AC3):** a proxy outage stops audit dispatch. The named reason and the operator-visible log are the mitigation; the one-release legacy escape hatch is the next child.
- **Assumption:** the proxy's `available` verdict is authoritative even when the dispatcher's local ledger disagrees — the local ledger becomes observability-only (reconciled in the next child's divergence log).

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.worker-contract.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.types.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-budget.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.downtime-select.test.ts`

## Impact

An audit is now admitted by the shared proxy's live capacity, so two ContextHub hosts can no longer each believe they are under their own per-host cap and overload the single local GPU.

# Admission choke point, divergence log and legacy flag

## Context

Parent: WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS — herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget.
Prerequisite: the audit gate reads proxy availability.

`admitHostDispatch` (`host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`) is the single admission reader both dispatcher paths funnel through once per dispatch attempt. Its header promises that "a refusal before selection and a refusal at admission agree" — so the audit branch must reach the same proxy-derived decision, not the local `maxAudit` cap.

## Scope

- `admitHostDispatch` audit branch: delegate to the proxy-derived decision (reuse `readAuditBudgetState`'s replacement from the previous child), so the pre-check and admission cannot disagree. Refusal tokens are the proxy's (`audit-budget-saturated`, `audit-budget-unknown`).
- Local ledger stays as **observability only** for the audit tier: the dispatch still reserves / confirms / releases its audit entry (so the worklist header, the interactive dialog, the closed-pane sweep and the release paths keep working unchanged), but the entry is never read to refuse an audit. Document that in the module header.
- Divergence log (AC2): when the proxy admits but the local fresh audit count is at/over `maxAudit`, or the proxy refuses while the local count is below the cap, write one decision-log entry naming both sides' evidence (`proxy: {live, cap, available}` vs `local: {live, maxAudit}`). No divergence → no entry (no log noise).
- One-release legacy escape hatch (AC3): env flag `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1` restores the pre-change behaviour (per-host `budget.json` `maxAudit` + local ledger) for the audit tier; read per tick, documented as one-release, with a removal note.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `admitHostDispatch({kind:'audit'})` refuses and admits on the proxy verdict only; a test drives both a permissive `budget.json` and a permissive proxy, then a saturated proxy, and proves the proxy decides.
- The pre-check and admission agree: a test pins that the same availability state yields the same admission answer through `getActiveAudit` and `admitHostDispatch`, and that the refusal token is identical on both sides (AC2).
- A divergence (proxy admits / local ledger at cap, and the inverse) writes exactly one decision-log entry carrying both sides' evidence; an agreeing state writes none.
- With `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET=1` the audit tier returns to the `budget.json` + local-ledger decision (existing `host-dispatch-budget.acceptance.test.ts` semantics), the proxy is not consulted, and a warning marks the legacy path in the log.
- The implement tier's admission and reservation behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged (existing tests pass unmodified; one new pin asserts the implement branch never reads the proxy).
- Audit entries are still reserved, confirmed and released locally (a test asserts the ledger entry lifecycle on both the admit and refuse paths), and the audit entry alone can never cause a refusal.
- Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC3 — Fail-safe on an unreachable proxy.** If the proxy cannot be reached, audit dispatch fails **closed** with a named reason (e.g. `audit-budget-unknown`) and logs the proxy error; the legacy local-ledger path remains behind an explicit flag for one release.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Replace the audit branch of `admitHostDispatch` with the proxy-derived decision + reservation-for-observability.
2. Add the divergence comparison and decision-log entry (`downtime-log-budget.ts` vocabulary).
3. Add the `HERDR_AUDIT_LOCAL_BUDGET` flag reader + legacy branch.
4. Extend `host-dispatch-budget.acceptance.test.ts` and `host-dispatch-budget.machine.test.ts` with the agreement/divergence/flag cases.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** one audit slot reservation in the local ledger per proxy-admitted dispatch keeps every existing release/sweep/header path valid; the header may therefore show `1/1` while the proxy admits a second audit — documented as observability-only in the next child (docs).
- **Risk:** a divergence means the two views disagree in production. The log entry is the evidence trail for the release decision; it never changes the admission answer (the proxy wins).

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log-budget.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.acceptance.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.machine.test.ts`

## Impact
Operators can trust that an audit is admitted by the shared proxy's live capacity — two ContextHub hosts can no longer each believe they are under their own per-host cap — with any proxy/local disagreement recorded alongside both sides' evidence, and a one-release flag to fall back to the old local decision.

# Cross-host audit serialisation acceptance proof

## Context

Parent: **WL-0MW95GBEG005ERHS** — herdr audit admission queries the proxy-managed budget.

The incident this parent exists to fix: two ContextHub hosts, each enforcing its own `maxAudit: 1`, produced two concurrent audits on the single local GPU (2026-11-03). Per-host unit tests cannot prove that is now impossible; a scenario with **two dispatcher instances sharing one stub proxy** can.

## Scope

An integration-level acceptance suite (`packages/herdr/src/audit-availability.cross-host.test.ts`) that runs two dispatcher admission paths against one in-process stub proxy implementing the pinned availability contract:

1. Host A is admitted (proxy `available: true`), the stub proxy then reports the live lease (`available: false`) — host B is refused with `audit-budget-saturated`.
2. Both hosts are refused with the same token and the same evidence (dispatcher and proxy agree) — the AC2 agreement at the cross-host level, not just per call.
3. The proxy is unreachable (stub closed) — both hosts fail closed with `audit-budget-unknown` and no pane spawn.
4. Stale-lease reclamation: the stub reports one lease already expired plus `available: true` — host B dispatches; the read reflects the proxy's reclamation rather than holding a phantom slot.
5. The implement tier on both hosts is unaffected by the stub's audit state (proxy switching from available to saturated changes no implement admission answer).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The suite drives two independent dispatcher instances through one stub proxy and asserts per-case: admission answer, refusal token, evidence and whether a spawn happened.
- Case 1 fails on the pre-change code (a regression pin: with per-host caps both hosts admit) and passes after the parent's change — the test documents the incident it prevents.
- Case 2 asserts the dispatcher's token equals the stub proxy's refusal reason string (`audit-budget-saturated`), proving one vocabulary.
- Case 3 asserts `audit-budget-unknown` on both hosts, no spawn, and the proxy error recorded in the decision log.
- Case 4 asserts dispatch proceeds when only expired leases are reported (reclamation reflected), with the lease evidence in the log.
- Case 5 asserts the implement tier's admission answers are identical before and after the stub's audit verdict changes.
- The suite needs no network access (the stub is in-process) and leaves no open handles.
- Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Tests cover: availability read maps to the dispatch decision; second audit refused with agreement between dispatcher and proxy; unreachable proxy fails closed; stale-lease reclamation reflected; the implement tier is unchanged. Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Minimal Implementation

1. Build the in-process stub proxy (an injected `fetcher` or a `node:http` server on port 0) implementing the pinned availability contract.
2. Wire two dispatch-gate instances through `createDowntimeDeps`-style seams with the stub as `readAuditAvailability`.
3. Cover the five scenarios with decision-log assertions.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the stub is the contract record — if the proxy's real shape differs, the stub and the pinned parser change together (one path constant + aliases), not the scenarios.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/audit-availability.cross-host.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-availability.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch-filter.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.gates.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/host-dispatch-budget.admission.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.fixtures.ts`

## Impact

Operators can now point to a single cross-host acceptance proof that two ContextHub hosts can no longer dispatch concurrent audits on the shared local GPU: once one host's audit lease is live, the second host is refused with the proxy's own `audit-budget-saturated` token, and an unreachable proxy stops audits on every host instead of silently falling back to per-host caps.

# herdr worklist: substituted critical-child root loses `childCount`, so the parent cannot be expanded and the critical child is unreachable

## Goal

A critical **child** work item whose root ancestor is pulled into the worklist by
critical-child root substitution must be reachable in the herdr Work Items pane:
the substituted root row must render an expand arrow and expand to show its
children, exactly as it does when the same root arrives from the browse feed.

## Problem

Observed 2026-11-12 in the live Work Items pane (`wD:p180`, worklog root
`/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog`):

```
    ⭐  🔓📋✅   LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS Serialise audits at the shared local resource… [plan_complete] ⭐ high
```

Two leading spaces where every expandable row renders `▶`/`▼`:

```
  ▶ ⭐  ⛔📋❌   LP-0MW7V14DN007F127 …
```

`LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK` (**Proxy owns the audit admission budget and exposes
availability**, `critical`, `open`, `intake_complete`) is a child of
`LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS`. The top level only renders root items
(`selectWorkItems`, `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` rootOnly gate), so
the child is only reachable by expanding its parent — and the parent cannot be
expanded, so the child never appears.

**Root cause.** `substituteCriticalRoots`
(`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts`) resolves a critical child's
ancestors through the in-process DB fast path (`db.get`) or the `wl show`
fallback (`fetchItemDetails`, `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts:306`). Neither
emits `childCount`; only the enrichments in `wl list` / `wl next` /
`wl worklist` do (e.g. the child read at `fetcher.api.ts:517`). With
`childCount === undefined` every expand path is gated off:

- `worklist.ts:271` — the arrow renders only when `childCount > 0`;
- `worklist.ts:1601` — `Tab` toggles only when `childCount > 0`;
- `worklist.ts:5329` — that `Tab` path is the only on-demand
  `fetchChildrenForItem` entry, so children are never even fetched.

**Reproduction** with the plugin's own source (no mocks), worklog root
`/home/rgardler/projects/llm/.worklog`:

```
root via substitution: present cc=undefined
critical child at top level: false
```

i.e. `mergeMandatoryAndSelect(browseWithoutRoot, allMandatory, 25,
fetchItemDetails)` returns the root with `childCount === undefined`. The same
root fetched normally carries `childCount: 9`.

**Trigger condition.** When the root does not win one of the `browseItemCount`
"other" slots (in the observed case `othersLimit = 0`: 24–25 mandatory rows in
a 25-item window), `mergeUniqueById(enrichedItems, substituted.mandatory)` has
no enriched copy to keep, and `ensureSubstitutedRoots` restores the substituted
(childCount-less) object. Whenever the root is *in* the browse window the
enriched copy wins and the arrow is correct — so the defect is window-pressure
dependent.

**Impact beyond display.** `getHerdrListHead` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts:527`)
feeds the downtime dispatcher the same `fetchNextItems` output. The list head
therefore offers the substituted root (here: no `risk`/`effort` → a
`risk-effort` dispatch) and never the release-blocking critical child, so the
child is invisible to both the operator and auto-dispatch. The data layer is
otherwise sound: `wl next -n 25` ranks the child #1 and
`wl show LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS --children --json` returns it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Substituted roots are expandable.** A root injected by
  `substituteCriticalRoots` carries the same `childCount` a browse/`wl list`
  fetch would give it, so `formatItemLine` renders `▶` for it.
- **AC2 — Children are reachable.** With the root substituted (browse feed
  deliberately without it), `Tab`/`Enter` on that row triggers the on-demand
  child fetch and the critical child renders underneath it.
- **AC3 — Regression test for the window-pressure case.** A unit test asserts
  that when `othersLimit === 0` and a critical child's root is only in the
  mandatory set, the returned root has `childCount > 0` and is expandable;
  a second test pins that the browse-sourced root keeps its enriched
  `childCount` (no double-count, no clobber).
- **AC4 — Dispatcher head parity.** A test asserts the Herdr list head
  (`getHerdrListHead` / `fetchNextItems`) exposes the same expandable root
  shape used for rendering, so display and dispatch cannot diverge.
- **AC5 — Docs.** The critical-child root substitution comment block in
  `fetcher.root-substitution.ts` (and the reachability contract note in
  `smart-selection.ts`) records that substituted roots must carry
  `childCount`, and why a stripped ancestor is unsafe.
- **AC6 — Tests.** Changed-scope tests pass via `/skill:test`; the full suite
  passes at the dev-push gate.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts` — `substituteCriticalRoots`
  / `walkToRootAncestor` ancestor lookups (`db.get`, injected `itemDetails`).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts` — `fetchItemDetails` (no `childCount`),
  `readChildrenInProcess` (already computes `db.getChildCounts(allRaw)` at
  line ~504 — the reusable source).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — expand affordances gated on `childCount`
  (lines 271, 1601, 5329).
- `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts` — new regression tests (AC3/AC4).

## Out of scope

- The rootOnly top-level rendering rule itself (`selectWorkItems`).
- Any `llm`-side change; this is a `packages/herdr` display/reachability defect.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `childCount` is the canonical "has children" signal for the
  expand affordance; two independent gates (`worklist.ts:1601`, `5329`) agree.
- **Risk:** counting children at ancestor-resolution time could add cost to a
  refresh. Mitigation: reuse the existing single-connection in-process
  `getChildCounts` pass rather than a per-item spawn, and fall back to leaving
  the arrow absent (today's behaviour) if the read fails — fail-open, never a
  crash.
- **Discovery:** found while investigating why `LP-0MW95FYMH006XYNK` (llm
  worklog) was absent from the herdr Work Items pane.

## Impact

The herdr Work Items pane now renders a substituted critical-child root with an expand arrow even under window pressure, so the critical child is reachable by expanding the root — in both the pane and the downtime dispatcher list head.
